title: Security by Design
summary: Plan layers of physical, digital, and procedural protection from the beginning of a design.
objectives: Identify physical, digital, and procedural security layers.
Explain why security should be considered during design rather than added afterward.

vocab.def: An approved ability to access or do something.
An area limited to people with an approved reason to enter.
An agreed sequence of steps for doing work safely and consistently.

sections.heading: Security has layers
sections.body: A design may include controlled building access, restricted zones, cameras, permissions, monitoring, strong passwords, and clear procedures. No single layer solves every risk.

sections.heading: Design for the people using it
sections.body: Good security makes approved work possible while limiting unnecessary access. Teams can ask who needs access, what they need to do, and how changes should be recorded.

sections.heading: Defensive classroom design
sections.body: Create a safe access plan for a paper facility. Do not bypass a lock, test a real system, or practice offensive cybersecurity. The goal is protection and responsible decision making.

practice.prompt: For a server room, choose one physical layer, one digital layer, and one procedure. Explain what risk each layer helps address.

quiz.question: Why include security during design?
options: Protection can be planned alongside systems and user needs
Security makes all other systems unnecessary
It guarantees that no incident can occur
quiz.answer: Protection can be planned alongside systems and user needs

reflectionPrompt: Which security layer would you want explained clearly before using a shared facility?
